transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because things at work have gotten… not right. I drive routes, and dispatch and compliance keep tracking my route changes through the computer system, and then there’ll be these little comments on the radio that sound like they’re about me. People say it’s just normal oversight, but I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me.

And it’s not like I don’t know how the system works—I’ve been doing transportation long enough, and honestly even back when I was taking classes, people always acted like paperwork explains everything, but it doesn’t. You can feel when people are watching what you do. So… yeah, that’s why I came in.
How long have you been noticing these feelings that coworkers are watching or reporting on you—days, weeks, or longer?

It’s been longer than days… I’d say about two months where it’s felt really clear. Like the computer tracking and then the radio comments lining up with it. Before that, I mean, work’s always had systems and people checking routes, that’s just transportation, you know—but these last couple months it’s been different.
Aside from the radio comments that actually happen, have you ever heard voices or other sounds that other people around you don't seem to hear?

I don’t think so… I mean, not like a voice standing next to me or anything. The radio is real, that’s on at work, and sometimes there are sounds in the yard or the trucks making noises, so it’s hard to say what other people notice. But I haven’t had, like… somebody talking to me when there’s nobody there. At least not that I can point to like that.

Before these last two months at work, have you generally had a long-standing pattern of distrusting people or suspecting others' motives in other areas of your life—like with friends or family—going back to your teenage years or earlier?

I don’t know… I mean, I wouldn’t say I’ve always been like that with everybody. Teenage years is kind of a long time ago, and back then I was mostly worried about school stuff and getting rides and who was saying what, like everybody was.

With family, it’s different because people have their own habits, you know? My aunt always had this way of acting like she knew what was best, and then you start noticing how people talk around things instead of saying them straight. But I don’t know if that’s the same as what you mean. I guess I’m not sure I’d call it a long-standing pattern. This work thing feels more specific.
Aside from the situation at work, has anything changed in how you're managing day-to-day things—like your sleep, self-care, or relationships with friends and family outside of work?

Yeah… I guess it has changed some. I mean, work bleeds into everything, you know? Like if the route reports aren’t right, then the drivers get irritated, and then I’m thinking about that at home while I’m supposed to be making dinner or calling someone back.

I’ve gotten behind on the reports, and sometimes the instructions I give the drivers come out confusing enough that they complain. Not on purpose, it’s just… there’s too many pieces moving around.

At home my husband’s been picking up a lot. Meals, phone calls, figuring out basic plans—like appointments or what we’re doing that week. I used to handle more of that, but lately I’m not keeping up like I normally would.
Have you noticed yourself feeling emotionally flat or less interested in things you used to enjoy, or pulling away from people you used to talk to, over these past couple months?

Yeah… I guess. I mean, I used to like choir, it was sort of the one thing where I didn’t have to think about schedules and dispatch stuff, just stand there and sing. But lately I don’t really feel like going, or even singing when I’m there.

And softball too—we used to have the team over sometimes after games, and I’d make snacks or whatever, but now that sounds like… too much noise, too much getting ready. Most days after my shift I just sit at the kitchen table with my planner open, like I’m going to start dinner or make calls or plan something, and then I just don’t. I just sit there staring at it.

Thinking back further, when did you first start noticing yourself pulling away from things like choir or softball, or losing interest in activities—was that around the same two months, or did it start earlier than the work suspicions?

I think it was… mostly around the same time, but it’s hard to separate it out because the calendar all kind of runs together. Like choir is on Thursdays, and I used to know that without even checking, and now I’ll look at the planner and it’s right there but I just don’t feel like singing. I keep thinking I’ll go next week.

Softball too, it’s not that I hate it or anything. We used to have people over after games, and I’d get chips and drinks and make space in the living room, but now that sounds like a whole production. Even little things feel like that. After my shift I’ll sit at the kitchen table with the planner open, like I’m going to start dinner or call someone back, and I just… don’t start. I just sit there.

So I don’t know if it came before exactly. I noticed it more once all this work stuff was already going on.
Over these past two months, how has your sleep been—are you having trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual?

I don’t know… I mean, I go to bed, but then I start thinking about whether I wrote something down wrong, or if there was something I was supposed to do the next day. But I don’t know if that’s “trouble sleeping” exactly.

Sometimes I’ll just lie there and hear the refrigerator making that clicking sound, and then I remember we need to clean behind it because my husband said that months ago, and then I’m thinking about whether I paid the electric bill, and it kind of goes in a circle.

I haven’t really kept track of the hours. I don’t think I’m sleeping a lot more than usual. It’s just… hard to say.

Have there been any days in these past two months where you felt fine—not down or withdrawn—but still had those strong suspicions about being watched or reported on, or times you felt depressed without those suspicions at all?

I mean… I don’t know if I’d separate it like that. There have been days where I’m not exactly sad, like I’m just getting through the route and doing what I’m supposed to do, but the dispatch stuff is still there. The computer system shows the route changes, and then compliance sees it, and then you hear these little comments on the radio that sound normal if you’re not paying attention, but they line up.

Like even if I’m in an okay mood, I can tell certain drivers are reporting back on me. People keep saying it’s just oversight, but it doesn’t feel like just oversight when the comments come right after something I did. So… yeah, it’s not only when I’m down. It’s more like the watching is happening either way.

It’s not really just a mood thing, I guess. I’m here because of the dispatch and compliance stuff—like the route changes don’t just disappear, they go through the computer system, and people can see that. And then there are these little comments on the radio that sound casual, but they come right after something I did.

I know people say it’s normal oversight, and I understand buses have to be tracked, but it’s more than that. Certain drivers are reporting back on me. I can tell by the timing. I don’t know how else to explain it.

Going back further, before these last two months, had you ever had a stretch—even briefly—where you felt people were watching or reporting on you in a similar way, or is this the very first time you've experienced this kind of suspicion?

I don’t think it was like this before. I mean, work always has tracking, everybody knows that, and drivers talk, dispatch talks… sometimes people make comments and you wonder what they mean, but I didn’t really think of it as being about me before.

This thing with the computer system and the radio comments feeling connected—like clearly connected—that’s been more like the last two months. Around then it started feeling obvious to me. Before that, I might’ve been annoyed with work stuff, but not… not this same feeling, I guess.
Since these suspicions started about two months ago, have they been present nearly every day since then, or have there been any breaks where you felt completely back to your usual self?

It’s been… I mean, pretty much since it started, yeah. The tracking through the computer system and the radio comments, that’s been clear to me for about the past two months.

There might be moments where I’m distracted, like if I’m dealing with passengers or trying to make a tight stop, or thinking about bills or my sister calling me about something, but it doesn’t feel like it’s gone. It’s still there in the background. I haven’t really had a stretch where I felt completely back to how I was before all this.

Yeah, like I said, it’s been about two months where it’s felt clear to me. The computer tracking and then the radio comments lining up with it… that’s when it stopped feeling like just normal work stuff.

I mean, buses have all kinds of systems now, and they’re always changing things around, even with the schedules and the little printer receipts and whatever—but this specific feeling, that it’s connected to me, that’s been about two months.

It’s… it’s really been about two months, like I was saying. That’s when the computer tracking and the stuff on the radio started feeling obvious to me, like it wasn’t just random work noise anymore.

I know I keep circling back to the buses and the systems, but that’s where it shows up. Around two months ago is when it became clear to me.

But I don’t know how to answer it cleanly. My mind kind of goes to work stuff—routes, timing, people watching, the radio—and then I lose the thread. Can you say that question again a little more directly?

Over the past two months, would you say the low mood and loss of interest have been present most of the time alongside the suspicions, or have there been a good number of days where you felt essentially okay mood-wise even though the suspicions were still there?

It’s not exactly like low mood every minute, I guess. It’s more like… I don’t really want to do the things I used to do.

Like choir—I used to sing, and softball, sometimes I’d have the team over after, you know, snacks and everyone talking too loud in the kitchen. I don’t feel like doing any of that now. Most days after my shift I just sit at the kitchen table with my planner open, and I mean to start dinner or call somebody or just do one thing, but I don’t. I just sit there looking at it.

So I don’t know if that’s “low mood” exactly, but I’m not really okay like I used to be.
Have you ever had a period—before or during these two months—where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than normal but didn't feel tired?

I don’t think so… I mean, not like feeling amazing or like I could do everything.

Sleep is weird sometimes because of my shifts, you know, early routes and late ones mess you up, and then if I drink coffee too late I’ll be up staring at the ceiling thinking about the next day’s schedule. But that’s not really the same thing, I guess. I still feel tired.

I can’t remember a time where I needed way less sleep and was fine. At least… nothing like that stands out.
In the past two months, have you had any thoughts of wanting to hurt yourself or end your life?

I… I don’t really know. I mean, I get really worn out and sometimes I just don’t want to deal with anything, but “end my life” sounds so… direct.

I haven’t been making plans or anything like that. Mostly I just kind of sit there and my mind goes in circles, like I’ll think about work and then the bills and then whether I left something undone, and then I lose track of what I was even upset about.

So… I don’t think I’ve had thoughts like that, not in a clear way. I just feel tired of everything sometimes.

I’m not sure what you mean exactly… like, if you mean a real plan or something, no, I don’t have that.

patient.answer:
I’m here because things at work have gotten… not right. I drive routes, and dispatch and compliance keep tracking my route changes through the computer system, and then there’ll be these little comments on the radio that sound like they’re about me. People say it’s just normal oversight, but I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me.

And it’s not like I don’t know how the system works—I’ve been doing transportation long enough, and honestly even back when I was taking classes, people always acted like paperwork explains everything, but it doesn’t. You can feel when people are watching what you do. So… yeah, that’s why I came in.
